scope_note: The severity table is supplied in the exhibit, so items test reading a real message against it rather than reciting it.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. Which part of this message names the facility that raised it?

exhibit.content:
A message arrives at the syslog server from a switch.

    %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/7,
    changed state to down

    Level  Keyword          Meaning
    -----  --------------   ------------------------------
      0    emergencies      system unusable
      1    alerts           immediate action needed
      2    critical         critical condition
      3    errors           error condition
      4    warnings         warning condition
      5    notifications    normal but significant
      6    informational    informational message
      7    debugging        debugging output

items.explanation: A syslog message is built as facility, then severity, then mnemonic, so LINEPROTO is the facility, 5 is the severity and UPDOWN is the mnemonic naming the specific event. Option A is that mnemonic. Option B is the severity, which places the message at notifications. Option D is a value from the message text, describing what the event concerns rather than which subsystem reported it.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. Which two of the four messages reach the syslog server? (Choose two.)

exhibit.content:
! R2 - relevant configuration
!
logging host 10.9.9.40
logging trap 4
!

Four messages are generated on R2 in the next minute:

    %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down
    %SYS-5-CONFIG_I: Configured from console by netadmin on vty0
    %OSPF-5-ADJCHG: Process 1, Nbr 2.2.2.2 on Gi0/1 from FULL to DOWN
    %SYS-2-MALLOCFAIL: Memory allocation of 4096 bytes failed

    Level  Keyword          Meaning
    -----  --------------   ------------------------------
      0    emergencies      system unusable
      1    alerts           immediate action needed
      2    critical         critical condition
      3    errors           error condition
      4    warnings         warning condition
      5    notifications    normal but significant
      6    informational    informational message
      7    debugging        debugging output

options.text: %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down
%SYS-5-CONFIG_I: Configured from console by netadmin on vty0
%OSPF-5-ADJCHG: Process 1, Nbr 2.2.2.2 on Gi0/1 from FULL to DOWN
None of them, since logging trap 4 excludes every level shown

items.explanation: logging trap 4 forwards everything at level 4 or more severe, and severity counts downward, so levels 0 through 4 are sent while 5 through 7 are discarded; that captures the level 3 link message and the level 2 memory failure. Options B and C both sit at level 5, notifications, and are dropped, which is how a trap level set too low silently loses configuration and adjacency changes. Option E inverts the scale, treating a higher number as more severe.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. Which message should be dealt with first, and why?

exhibit.content:
Two messages arrive within the same second from the same router.

    %SYS-2-MALLOCFAIL: Memory allocation of 4096 bytes failed
    %SYS-6-LOGGINGHOST_STARTSTOP: Logging to host 10.9.9.40 started

    Level  Keyword          Meaning
    -----  --------------   ------------------------------
      0    emergencies      system unusable
      1    alerts           immediate action needed
      2    critical         critical condition
      3    errors           error condition
      4    warnings         warning condition
      5    notifications    normal but significant
      6    informational    informational message
      7    debugging        debugging output

options.text: The LOGGINGHOST message, since level 6 outranks level 2 on this scale.
Neither is urgent; both sit in the routine half of the severity range.
Both equally, as messages from one facility carry the same weight.
The MALLOCFAIL message, because level 2 is nearer the severe end.

items.explanation: Severity runs from 0 as the most serious to 7 as the least, so the level 2 memory allocation failure is a critical condition while the level 6 logging notice is informational housekeeping. Option A reads the scale backwards, which is the mistake this item exists to catch. Option B places level 2 in the routine half, when the table marks it critical. Option C treats the shared SYS facility as making them equivalent, but the facility says which subsystem spoke rather than how much it matters.

items.stem: Refer to the exhibit. At which severity level was this message recorded?

exhibit.content:
A message recorded on the syslog server

    %SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP: list 110 denied tcp 10.20.4.55(51204) ->
    10.90.1.10(22), 1 packet

    Level  Keyword          Meaning
    -----  --------------   ------------------------------
      0    emergencies      system unusable
      1    alerts           immediate action needed
      2    critical         critical condition
      3    errors           error condition
      4    warnings         warning condition
      5    notifications    normal but significant
      6    informational    informational message
      7    debugging        debugging output

items.explanation: The severity is the number between the facility and the mnemonic, so SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP is level 6, informational, which is the usual level for an access list logging a match. Option A is the access list number taken from the message text. Option B and option D are severities that appear nowhere in this message; the value 1 is the packet count at the end of the line, which is a different number entirely.
